description: Solo participant, IT graduate working on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data using Python
summary: Oman Burning Calendar harmonizes two NASA FIRMS active fire records, MODIS and VIIRS, into one consistent monthly history for Oman from January 2012 to August 2026. VIIRS has a finer pixel (375 m vs 1 km) and detects about 21.9 times more hotspots per month than MODIS, so the two cannot be compared directly. I scaled VIIRS counts to the MODIS level using the median monthly ratio, so the sensor of origin no longer matters. The result is a colorblind-friendly burning activity calendar (year by month), an interactive page to choose years and compare any month with its typical level, and a downloadable CSV of the harmonized counts. It helps emergency managers and land managers see seasonal patterns and unusual months at a glance. The method is simple, and its limits are documented.
details:
What it does: Oman Burning Calendar turns two separate NASA FIRMS fire records, MODIS and VIIRS, into one consistent monthly history of active fire hotspots over Oman (Jan 2012 to Aug 2026).

How it works: MODIS (1 km pixel) and VIIRS S-NPP (375 m pixel) cannot be compared directly, because VIIRS detects about 21.9 times more hotspots per month (median ratio, range 10.6 to 67.1). I divided VIIRS counts by this factor to put both sensors on the MODIS scale, then counted hotspots per month. After scaling, the monthly series correlate at 0.61.

Outputs: a colorblind-friendly burning activity calendar (year by month), an interactive page to choose years and series and compare any month with its typical level (median), and a downloadable CSV of the harmonized monthly counts.

Impact: Emergency and land managers can quickly see seasonal patterns, busy periods and unusual months without worrying about which satellite produced the data.

Tools: Python, pandas, matplotlib, Jupyter, VS Code, HTML/CSS/JavaScript.

Limits: one scale factor cannot fit every month; hotspots include gas flares and industrial heat, not only wildfires; Jan 2012 is a partial month; the tool covers all of Oman, not sub-regions.
